issue.title: fix(auth): media_viewer_context rejects BUD-01 get events on blob routes
issue.body:
## Summary

`media_viewer_context` rejects BUD-01 (kind 24242) auth events with `['t', 'get']` on blob GET routes. All viewer handlers (blob, HLS master, HLS content, thumbnail, subtitle, audio, quality variant) use `media_viewer_context` -> `diagnose_viewer_auth` -> `diagnose_viewer_auth_request`, which calls `validate_viewer_event`. For BUD-01 events, this dispatches to `validate_blossom_event(event, AuthAction::List)` -- only accepting `['t', 'list']`.

The correct validation path exists: `validate_blob_viewer_event` -> `validate_blossom_get_event` accepts `['t', 'get']` with hash verification. But it's only reachable through `authenticate_blob_viewer`, which is called by `viewer_pubkey` in `auth.rs` -- a function none of the viewer handlers use.

## Impact

Clients sending BUD-01 get events for age-restricted blob fetches get 401 despite valid auth. divine-web worked around this by switching to NIP-98 (kind 27235) in divinevideo/divine-web#348.

## Fix

`diagnose_viewer_auth_request` should detect blob paths (via `blob_hash_from_path`) and dispatch BUD-01 events to `validate_blob_viewer_event` instead of `validate_viewer_event`, matching the logic already in `viewer_pubkey`.

~4 lines changed. No breaking changes -- strictly additive. NIP-98 unaffected, BUD-01 list events unaffected, non-blob paths unaffected.

## Relevant code

- `src/viewer_auth.rs:271` -- `diagnose_viewer_auth_request` calls `validate_viewer_event`
- `src/viewer_auth.rs:146` -- `validate_viewer_event` uses `AuthAction::List` for BUD-01
- `src/viewer_auth.rs:162` -- `validate_blob_viewer_event` uses `AuthAction::Get` for BUD-01 (correct)
- `src/auth.rs:36-55` -- `viewer_pubkey` does the right blob path dispatch but isn't used by viewer handlers

issue.title: feat: Implement actual thumbnail extraction
issue.body:
### Summary

`extract_video_thumbnail` in `cloud-functions/process-blob/main.py` is a stub: it logs a TODO and always returns `None`. Video uploads therefore never get a real thumbnail for moderation or metadata until this is implemented.

### Problem / Motivation

  `extract_video_thumbnail` in `cloud-functions/process-blob/main.py` is still a
   stub: it logs a TODO and always returns `None`. For `video/*` uploads that means:
  - No JPEG frame is produced or uploaded for moderation.
  - The pipeline falls through to `update_metadata(..., status='pending', ...)` instead of
  running Vision SafeSearch on a thumbnail.
  - Downstream UX (thumbnails at the edge, metadata `thumbnail` field, deleting a thumbnail
   when content is restricted) cannot behave as intended until real extraction exists.

### Proposed Approach

  1. Implement frame extraction from the source video (e.g. `ffmpeg` or equivalent),
  writing a single JPEG to a temp file, then uploading it to the same GCS bucket as the
  source object.
  2. Return the resulting GCS object key from `extract_video_thumbnail` so existing callers
   stay unchanged: `check_image_safety(bucket_name, thumbnail_path)` already uses
  `gs://{bucket}/{blob_name}` for Vision.
  3. Align the **uploaded object key** with how the app serves thumbnails (`{sha256}.jpg`
  vs the current stub `thumbnails/{blob_name}`) so Fastly/Rust (`parse_thumbnail_path`,
  `download_thumbnail`) and the metadata webhook stay consistent.
  4. Extend the `Dockerfile` or chosen runtime
   to include whatever binary/library is required; today only `c2patool` is installed—no
  `ffmpeg` yet.
  5. Ensure extracted `.jpg` objects are ignored by `_is_generated_derivative` / naming
  rules so processing does not recurse on generated thumbnails.
  6. Add or adjust tests around `extract_video_thumbnail` success/failure and the video
  branch of `process_blob_event`.

### Additional Context

  - TODO location: `extract_video_thumbnail`
   https://github.com/divinevideo/divine-blossom/blob/55caf2c5774548f01ed30ed795d384f7d82e976a/cloud-functions/process-blob/main.py#L416
  - Video flow: `process_blob_event` calls extraction, then moderation +
  `handle_moderation_result` with optional `thumbnail_path` for cleanup on flag.
  - Operational limits: gunicorn `--timeout 300` in the Dockerfile; large videos may need
  download/size/time guards analogous to C2PA limits.

issue.title: fix: cached 404s persist after moderation status change (Compute cache not purged)
issue.body:
## Problem

When a blob's moderation status changes (e.g., Restricted → Active via `/admin/moderate`), the Fastly Compute cache at `media.divine.video` continues serving the stale response. Quarantine-to-active transitions serve cached 404s; active-to-quarantine transitions serve cached 200s.

Both directions are broken:
- **Active → Restricted**: moderated content remains publicly accessible via CDN
- **Restricted → Active**: approved content returns 404 until cache naturally expires

## Root cause

Two gaps in the cache purge path:

1. **`error_response()` sets no cache headers or surrogate key.** Success responses get `Surrogate-Key: {hash}` via `add_cache_headers()`, but 404 responses for restricted/banned blobs go through `error_response()` which sets none. Fastly caches them under default rules, and surrogate-key purge can't target them.

2. **`purge_vcl_cache()` targets the website, not the media CDN.** It purges VCL service `ML7R82HKfmTaqTpHExIDVN` (divine.video website), not the Compute service `pOvEEWykEbpnylqst1KTrR` (media.divine.video). The Compute service's cache is never purged after moderation actions.

## Verified

- Origin (edgecompute URL) serves 200 correctly after SAFE action
- `media.divine.video` continues serving cached 404 (`age` growing, `x-cache: MISS` from edge hitting stale shield)
- HTTP `PURGE` method against `media.divine.video/{sha256}` clears the Compute cache immediately
- Fastly API surrogate-key purge against the Compute service does not clear cached 404s (no surrogate key on 404 response)

## Proposed fix

1. Add `Surrogate-Key: {hash}` and short-TTL `Surrogate-Control` to access-denied 404 responses for known blobs, so cached 404s are purgeable and expire quickly
2. Add a Compute-service self-purge (HTTP PURGE to `media.divine.video/{hash}`) in the `/admin/moderate` handler alongside the existing VCL purge

issue.title: refactor(core): extract a blossom-core lib crate for native test execution
issue.body:
## Problem

All `#[test]` functions in `delete_policy.rs`, `blossom.rs`, and `error.rs` are pure Rust with no Fastly SDK dependency, but `cargo test` fails because the linker can't resolve Fastly's host-call FFI symbols on macOS/Linux. There is no `fastly compute test` subcommand (checked CLI v14.3.1). Tests are currently compile-verified only via `cargo check --tests --target wasm32-wasip1`.

## Proposal

Create a `blossom-core` workspace member (lib crate) containing:
- `BlossomError` / `Result` (replace `fastly::http::StatusCode` with `http::StatusCode` -- same type, both http v1.4.0)
- `BlobStatus`, `BlobMetadata`, and related domain types from `blossom.rs` (zero Fastly imports)
- Pure policy functions from `delete_policy.rs` (`validate_sha256_format`, `map_moderate_action`, `handle_creator_delete_with_ops`, `build_creator_delete_response`, etc.)
- All associated tests (~80 across three modules)

The main binary crate re-exports everything via `pub use blossom_core::*`, so existing `crate::blossom::*` and `crate::error::*` import paths keep working. Fastly-dependent functions (`soft_delete_blob`, `restore_soft_deleted_blob`, `DefaultCreatorDeleteOps`) stay in the binary crate.

## Outcome

`cargo test -p blossom-core` runs all pure-logic tests natively. No Viceroy, no WASM target, standard `cargo test` output with filtering.

## Dependencies

Depends on #103 landing first (adds the `validate_sha256_format` / `map_moderate_action` extraction + tests).

issue.title: Blob metadata-None bypasses access control in handle_get_blob and handle_head_hls_content
issue.body:
## Summary

When KV metadata is `None` for a blob, `handle_get_blob` skips access control entirely and serves content directly from GCS. `handle_head_hls_content` has the same gap, leaking blob existence via HEAD.

Exploitable when metadata is deleted but GCS bytes remain -- which happens when `vanish` runs on a pubkey whose blobs were already removed from the user list by a prior soft-delete. Discovered Apr 30 exercising the content removal pathway.

## Root cause

The `if let Some(ref meta) = metadata` pattern has been in `handle_get_blob` since the initial implementation (Dec 2025). Originally safe -- `None` metadata just meant "pre-KV-tracking upload" and no moderation system existed. Became a security gap when moderation actions that delete metadata (`vanish`) were added alongside GCS bytes that can outlive their metadata.

The Apr 10 `access_for` refactor (`af76383`) audited all 14 gate sites but focused on consolidating status logic, not the `None` path. Endpoints where the compiler forced an unwrap (downstream code needed metadata fields) got the safe `ok_or_else(NotFound)` pattern. `handle_get_blob` didn't -- it serves bytes from GCS without needing metadata -- so the compiler never complained and the `None` fallthrough survived.

## Fix

Branch `fix/metadata-none-access-control`:

1. `handle_get_blob`: `None` metadata returns 404 for non-admin requests, allows admin (needed for preview of orphaned blobs).
2. `handle_head_hls_content`: `None` metadata returns 404 (HEAD has no auth context).

All other blob-serving endpoints audited and confirmed safe.

review.body:
Same pattern as the fixes in #110 — `if let Ok(Some(...))` → `match get_blob_metadata()?` with explicit None arm. KV errors fail closed, None returns 404 for non-admin, admin bypass preserved for moderation proxy.

Comments are clear, scope is tight. Good to go.

issue.title: fix: return 404 when blob metadata is None for non-admin requests
issue.body:
Refs #109

## Summary

Fixes the metadata-None access-control bypass in the following blob-serving paths:

- `handle_get_blob` main blob path: `None` metadata now returns 404 for non-admin requests and allows admin preview of orphaned blobs.
- `handle_head_hls_content`: `None` metadata now returns 404 instead of falling through to HEAD existence checks.
- `handle_get_blob` thumbnail subpath: `if let Ok(Some(...))` now uses explicit metadata handling so `None` returns 404 for non-admin requests and KV errors propagate as 5xx.
- `handle_get_subtitle_by_hash`: `None` metadata no longer falls through to subtitle job lookup.
- `handle_head_blob` thumbnail path: now applies metadata-based access control before returning 200 plus `Content-Length`.

The remaining same-class path, `handle_get_hls_content`, is fixed separately in #111.

## Root cause

When KV metadata is missing (for example after `vanish` deletes metadata but GCS bytes survive), the original `if let Some(...)` / `if let Ok(Some(...))` patterns skipped access control entirely and fell through to storage-backed responses.

Several of those sites were also swallowing KV errors as “no metadata, allow” rather than failing closed.

## Scope

This PR fixes the metadata-None bypass everywhere listed above.

`handle_get_hls_content` is intentionally left to #111 to avoid duplicate commits. The full issue #109 remediation is the combination of #110 and #111.

## Test plan

- `cargo check --tests` passes (CI equivalent for Fastly Compute crate)
- `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features` clean
- CI green
- [ ] Deploy to staging and verify:
  - blob with no metadata returns 404 for non-admin requests
  - admin bearer token still bypasses for orphaned blob preview
  - thumbnail GET/HEAD for deleted metadata returns 404 for non-admin requests
  - subtitle-by-hash no longer returns job data when metadata is missing

comment.body:
@NotThatKindOfDrLiz Pushed 27f30ae addressing the three remaining paths from your review:

1. **thumbnail subpath** (`handle_get_blob`): `if let Ok(Some(meta))` → `match get_blob_metadata()?` with explicit None arm. KV errors now propagate as 5xx.
2. **subtitle-by-hash**: same pattern change — None no longer falls through to subtitle job lookup.
3. **HEAD thumbnail** (`handle_head_blob`): added metadata gate with `access_for(None, false)` before the `download_thumbnail` call.

`handle_get_hls_content` is covered by Ira's #111 — left it there rather than cherry-picking to avoid duplicate commits.

Removed the "all other endpoints audited and confirmed safe" claim from the PR body. Updated summary lists each path explicitly.

review.body:
The two changed call sites are fixed correctly, but I can't approve this as closing #109 because the same `metadata=None` fall-through pattern still exists in other blob-serving paths and the PR body explicitly says they were audited and safe.

Please extend this PR to cover the remaining same-class sites with the same explicit `match get_blob_metadata(...)?` / `None => 404 or admin-bypass` pattern, and avoid `if let Ok(Some(...))` so KV errors propagate as 5xx instead of silently bypassing access control.

The remaining paths I verified are:

1. `handle_get_blob` thumbnail subpath: still `if let Ok(Some(meta)) = get_blob_metadata(video_hash)` and then falls through to `download_thumbnail` / `generate_thumbnail_on_demand` on `None` or KV error.
2. `handle_get_hls_content`: still `if let Ok(Some(ref meta)) = get_blob_metadata(&hash)` and then falls through to `download_hls_content`.
3. `handle_get_subtitle_by_hash`: only applies access control if metadata is `Some(meta)`; if metadata is `None`, the next `if let Some(job)` returns subtitle job JSON without any access check.

Separately, `handle_head_blob`'s thumbnail path has no metadata gate at all before returning 200 + `Content-Length`, so it still leaks thumbnail existence. If you don't want to fix that in this PR, please drop the `all other blob-serving endpoints audited and confirmed safe` claim and file a follow-up issue for the `HEAD /{hash}.jpg` path.

comment.body: This `ok_or_else(NotFound)` fix is the right pattern, but the same fall-through issue still exists in `handle_get_hls_content` (`if let Ok(Some(ref meta)) = get_blob_metadata(&hash)`) and in `handle_get_subtitle_by_hash` (access control only runs when metadata is `Some(meta)`, then `if let Some(job)` returns job JSON on `None`). Please extend this PR to those call sites with the same explicit `match get_blob_metadata(...)?` shape so `None` is denied and KV errors stay 5xx.

This non-thumbnail `match metadata` fix is correct, but the same handler still has the vulnerable thumbnail branch above (`if let Ok(Some(meta)) = get_blob_metadata(video_hash)` at the `/{hash}.jpg` path). That branch still falls through to `download_thumbnail` / `generate_thumbnail_on_demand` when metadata is `None` or KV errors, so the access-control bypass remains for thumbnail bytes. Please fold that branch into this PR too instead of claiming the other blob-serving endpoints were audited and safe.

review.body:
Approved.

This is now doing the right thing end to end: the pure types and policy helpers move into `blossom-core`, the current post-#103 moderation contract is preserved there, and CI now actually runs the native `blossom-core` test suite instead of only compile-checking it.
